display.title: Reb Levik's Secret Chuppah
display.summary_short: For Vov Tishrei, a memory of Rebbetzin Chana, then the story of a secret midnight chuppah in Soviet Yekaterinoslav that brought a Communist informer back to Yiddishkeit.
display.summary_long: On Vov Tishrei, the yahrzeit of Rebbetzin Chana, the Rebbe's mother, the storyteller remembers holding the heavy door of her President Street building open for her as a young boy in Crown Heights, and how she once thanked him with a pat on the shoulder. The story goes back to Yekaterinoslav, where her husband, Rabbi Levi Yitzchak, was the Rav under Communist rule. Late one night, during the curfew, an old woman knocks softly: her daughter, who works in a Communist office, is marrying a Jewish young man and will agree to a kosher chuppah only if it is secret and performed by Reb Levik. He slips out through the streets to gather a minyan but is one man short, so he wakes Chaim, the Jewish superintendent downstairs, a Communist who reports on his visitors. Chaim agrees to come. After the joyful chuppah and l'chaim, Chaim stays behind in tears, hands Reb Levik his party card, and says, 'From today I am one of yours.' He does teshuvah and becomes a Chassid, moved by the mesiras nefesh he saw.
display.lesson: Mesiras nefesh for a mitzvah can touch even a heart that seems far away; and it is a privilege to help and honor elders.
